Column 'lat' directly maps to 'latitudeDecimal'.
Column 'lon' directly maps to 'longitudeDecimal'.
A location typically has a geometry, and we will link to a Point with lat/lon.

Column 'timestamp' directly maps to 'observationDateTime'.
The 'timestamp' column provides a snapshot time, matching the Observation class and its 'observationDateTime' property.
Column 'speed' is in knots, but the property is in m/s; however, the mapping is reasonable as a speed value.
Column 'course' is the absolute bearing angle of the vessel's movement.
Columns 'speed', 'heading', 'course' relate to velocity: speed, bearing, inclination.
Column 'heading' directly maps to 'headingAngle'.
Column 'heading' indicates the vessel's heading angle, mapping to Orientation.
Column 'max_speed' directly maps to 'vesselMaximumSpeed'.
Column 'flag' provides a two-letter country code, matching 'geopoliticalAffiliationCode'.
Column 'ship_country' may indicate the country operating the vessel, mapping to 'hasOperator' via a GeopoliticalAffiliation.
No clear column indicates ownership; 'ship_country' might imply affiliation rather than ownership.
Column 'imo' provides an IMO number, a standard alternate identifier value.
The IMO number implies a standard code 'IMO', which can be set based on context.
Column 'ship_id' is an internal identifier for the vessel.
No explicit standard code is given; assume a generic code based on source.
